can anything else get hurt, other than consumers of the log interface, by this move?
can anything else get hurt, other than consumers of the log interface, by this move?

Yes, one thing that matters, plus three small ones (checked at faee074). (1) THE BIG ONE: node.db rebuilds itself FROM the log. nodeStore.js:329-331: 'every hash here is also in traffic.jsonl. Losing node.db costs a rebuild, not the protection.' Put the log inside node.db and losing that one file loses the log AND the thing it would be rebuilt from. The fix is cheap: the log gets its own database file, say relay-state/traffic.db, not a table in node.db. That changes R19.1's wording. (2) Two tests read the file directly, not through the interface: liveFrontDoor.js:88 and measureCapacity.js:322. They'd be rewritten, and README/CAPACITY.md measures traffic.jsonl's size. (3) The cost of a write: today one line is appended per packet, afterwards one database commit per packet. Probably fine, but it should be measured, not assumed. (4) The existing file is imported once. After that, traffic.jsonl is read-once legacy, as traffic.json already is (trafficLog.js:115). Nothing outside the node is touched, and the agents app already refuses to read the node's log (agentsApp.js:305).
